A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Probably Approximately Precision and Recall Learning. All sections, detailed proofs, figures, and references support comparison. Neither version contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical algorithms, guarantees, proofs, and illustrative constructions, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout. Its additional application examples and discussion do not report empirical investigations.

M1.justification: The maximum-likelihood, truncated maximum-likelihood, surrogate-loss, and semi-realizable algorithms retain their procedures. Replacing graph neighborhoods with set-valued hypotheses expresses the same learning approach; the expanded algorithm descriptions restate existing material.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. The added medical, language-generation, and photo-tagging examples are motivation, not newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version contains empirical comparator evaluations. ERM and the proposed learning rules remain subjects of theoretical analysis; the new citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are added or revised. The theoretical sampling model still observes one uniformly sampled positive label per IID input. F1/Fβ objectives are discussed without an evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary experiments. The illustrative examples and lower-bound constructions are retained under the revised terminology.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. PAC confidence guarantees and concentration arguments remain theoretical rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical outcome entries are added, removed, or revised. The illustrative numerical losses and principal theorem guarantees remain unchanged, including the factor-5 upper bound and 1.05 lower bound for agnostic scalar loss.

T1.justification: Section 4 replaces the upper bound ℓ_scalar(g) ≤ d_H(gtarget,g) with ℓ_scalar(g) ≤ 2d_H(gtarget,g) + min_{g'∈H}ℓ_scalar(g'), a substantive local mathematical revision. The principal theorem guarantees and proof structure remain intact. A new transcription error in Theorem 1's proof subtracts gtarget(x_i), a set, where v1 subtracts its cardinality n_gtarget(x_i).

C1.justification: The central claims about positive-only learning, ERM failure, optimal realizable sample complexity, and agnostic multiplicative approximation are retained. Section 6 newly claims extensions of hardness results and realizable optimization guarantees to F1/Fβ objectives, modestly broadening the stated applicability.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the restriction to counting-measure precision and recall and leaves broader measures open. It also interprets F1/Fβ optima as particular Pareto-front points and adds a connection between precision/recall failures and hallucination/mode collapse. These qualifications and interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Neither version provides experimental implementation details, hardware, training configurations, or code/data access instructions. The expanded theoretical algorithm summaries do not disclose a new implementation or reproducibility resource.

R1.justification: v2 adds four references: DT21, Gol67, KM24, and KMV24. These extend the positioning toward reliable classification and language identification/generation. It also uses the existing SBLBG18 citation to discuss alternatives to counting measure; the broader related-work account is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening motivation are extensively rewritten, and the document systematically shifts from recommender-system graphs to general set-valued prediction. Section 3 gains labeled algorithm explanations and formulas previously developed later, while the discussion is expanded. This substantially revises the narrative despite retaining the section sequence and algorithms.

P2.justification: All three figures are retained. Figure 1 moves and changes its empty/complete graph labels to set labels; Figure 2's caption adopts set-function terminology; Figure 3's panel captions are reformatted. Equations and algorithm boxes undergo limited reflow, without new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves accessibility through its set-function framing and explicit algorithm summaries, and qualifies the overly strong surrogate-loss bound in Section 4. These gains are limited by the largely unchanged theoretical development, an F1/Fβ hardness extension asserted without a supporting derivation, and the new set/cardinality typo in Theorem 1's proof. Overall, the clarification and corrected bound provide a modest net improvement.
